mechanisms.definition: Asset identity is a stable schema identifier separate from node identity, coordinates and lineage.
mechanisms.integration: Allows one immutable asset to be instanced by many scene nodes.

mechanisms.definition: Canonical mesh/material/source metadata are hashed so derived geometry can be cached and compared.
mechanisms.integration: Cache key and integrity check; not a legal or cryptographic identity claim.

mechanisms.definition: Nodes form an explicit parent-child transform graph with local and world transforms.
mechanisms.integration: Supports conventional scene composition while UGTS events remain authoritative for changes.

mechanisms.definition: Parent edits are accepted only when the scene graph remains acyclic.
mechanisms.formula: parent walk must not revisit a node
mechanisms.integration: Prevents undefined world transforms and recursive editor corruption.

mechanisms.definition: Mesh/material assets are immutable payloads; nodes carry transform, visibility, tags and lineage.
mechanisms.integration: Allows reuse and streaming without treating render meshes as identity.

mechanisms.definition: Ordered layers may override declared node fields without destructively rewriting the base scene.
mechanisms.integration: Reference form of non-destructive authoring and variant overrides.

mechanisms.definition: Every scene declares up axis, handedness and working coordinate convention.
mechanisms.integration: Prevents silent axis flips across engine, glTF, USD and XR adapters.

mechanisms.definition: Linear scale, time unit and working color space are schema fields.
mechanisms.integration: Separates authored values from implicit engine defaults.

mechanisms.definition: World bounds map deterministically to one or more spatial cells.
mechanisms.integration: Supplies world partition and asynchronous loading keys.

mechanisms.definition: Version changes append an explicit from/to migration entry and description.
mechanisms.integration: Makes save-game and asset upgrades inspectable and replay-safe.

mechanisms.definition: Cubic Bezier segments subdivide until a declared flatness tolerance or depth limit is reached.
mechanisms.integration: Produces render/collision polylines from authoritative curves.

mechanisms.mechanism: Dual simulation and presentation error contract
mechanisms.definition: Derived geometry records independent world, collision, screen-space and normal error budgets.
mechanisms.integration: Prevents visually acceptable meshes from silently redefining event geometry.

mechanisms.definition: Closed 2D paths use an explicitly selected winding rule for interior classification.
mechanisms.integration: Supports vector fills, guards and hit regions without ambiguous self-intersections.

mechanisms.definition: An open polyline is compiled to a ribbon mesh with explicit width and join policy.
mechanisms.integration: Reference path-to-triangle conversion for editor and runtime previews.

mechanisms.definition: A profile ring is swept along a sampled 3D path to form a triangle mesh.
mechanisms.integration: Makes 2.0 curve families renderable and exportable.

mechanisms.definition: Rotation-minimizing tangent/normal/binormal frames orient profiles across low-curvature sections.
mechanisms.integration: Avoids Frenet flips at near-zero curvature.

mechanisms.definition: A bounded 3D lattice samples a declared scalar field and iso value.
mechanisms.integration: Input stage for deterministic field-to-mesh compilation.

mechanisms.definition: Each voxel cube is decomposed into tetrahedra and crossing edges are triangulated.
mechanisms.integration: Reference isosurface compiler with bounded resolution and no hidden raymarch loop.

mechanisms.definition: Analytic gradients are preferred; finite differences supply a bounded fallback.
mechanisms.integration: Supplies lighting orientation and diagnostic residuals.

mechanisms.definition: Tube vertices receive angular and cumulative-length coordinates.
mechanisms.integration: Provides stable procedural material coordinates.

mechanisms.definition: A derived axis-aligned proxy mesh is emitted from authoritative bounds.
mechanisms.integration: Allows inexpensive broad-phase and fallback collision.

mechanisms.definition: Triangle subsets form deterministic lower-detail previews with explicit topology-preservation status.
mechanisms.integration: Reference only; production simplification must preserve application error contracts.

mechanisms.definition: Each renderable or support volume may expose finite minimum/maximum bounds.
mechanisms.integration: Common currency for culling, broad phase and streaming.

mechanisms.definition: An optional local frame and half-extents describe tighter oriented bounds.
mechanisms.integration: Specified for production adapters; reference runtime falls back to AABB.

mechanisms.definition: A median split along the longest axis builds an inspectable hierarchy.
mechanisms.integration: Conventional acceleration complements UGTS support predicates.

mechanisms.definition: BVH overlap results pass through local-support predicates before exact relation work.
mechanisms.integration: Preserves the canonical support -> compatibility -> guard order.

mechanisms.definition: AABB positive vertices are tested against declared view planes.
mechanisms.formula: visible iff dot(n,p_positive)+d >= 0 for all planes
mechanisms.integration: Downstream view selection only; visibility does not change identity.

mechanisms.definition: Slab intervals return ordered AABB ray candidates.
mechanisms.integration: Editor picking and coarse interaction support.

mechanisms.definition: Object bounds enumerate every intersected regular-grid cell.
mechanisms.integration: Reference partition key for load/unload policies.

mechanisms.definition: Spatial overlap and required tags define a player/client interest set.
mechanisms.formula: interest={e: bounds(e) intersects query and tags_required subset tags(e)}
mechanisms.integration: Supports replication and streaming scope.

mechanisms.definition: Every rejected item reports frustum, support or compatibility cause.
mechanisms.integration: Makes editor and performance diagnostics actionable.

mechanisms.definition: Versioned numeric opcodes select pattern/field evaluators in coherent shader batches.
mechanisms.integration: GPU target keeps the 2.0 parameterized operator model.

mechanisms.definition: Instances store aligned offsets into a validated parameter buffer rather than inflating every hot record.
mechanisms.integration: Supports compact instancing and schema hashing.

mechanisms.definition: Bit flags declare analytic position, tangent, curvature, gradient or Hessian support.
mechanisms.integration: Missing derivatives select a declared numerical path.

mechanisms.definition: Passes declare read/write resources, queue class and dependency edges.
mechanisms.integration: Specified bridge from query results to raster/compute presentation.

mechanisms.definition: Visible instances may be compacted into indirect draw or mesh-dispatch commands.
mechanisms.integration: Production target; CPU reference emits ordinary SVG triangles.

mechanisms.definition: GPU kernels may append bounded event proposals with residual, status and confidence.
mechanisms.integration: Gameplay state is not committed by an unchecked shader write.

mechanisms.definition: Verified proposals are ordered by time, priority, source and proposal ID before state patches.
mechanisms.integration: Separates parallel detection from authoritative lineage change.

mechanisms.definition: Native target declares Vulkan 1.4-compatible resource, shader and timestamp contracts.
mechanisms.formula: backend=vulkan; physical_gpu_claim requires named device metrics
mechanisms.integration: No physical-GPU benchmark is claimed by this package.

mechanisms.definition: Portable target expresses compute and presentation kernels in WGSL-compatible layouts.
mechanisms.integration: Prototype shader supplied; browser/device execution remains target-specific.

mechanisms.definition: A deterministic camera, painter-order triangle pass and preview shader emit inspectable SVG.
mechanisms.integration: Regression oracle and demonstrator, not a production renderer.

mechanisms.definition: Base color, metallic, roughness, emissive and alpha mode have bounded ranges.
mechanisms.integration: Maps directly to common runtime asset conventions.

mechanisms.definition: Material graphs may read phase, curvature, arc length, sheet or pattern coordinates.
mechanisms.integration: Allows 2.0 patterns to drive masks and appearance.

mechanisms.definition: Small typed nodes evaluate constants, patterns, add, multiply, mix and clamp operations.
mechanisms.integration: Reference graph with explicit cycle rejection.

mechanisms.definition: Material evaluation is presentation-only and cannot mutate authoritative substrate state.
mechanisms.formula: material_output -> pixels; state change -> guard/event only
mechanisms.integration: Preserves the core reading rule.

mechanisms.definition: Lights declare kind, direction/color/intensity and shadow intent.
mechanisms.integration: Reference renderer implements one directional preview light; production shadows remain downstream.

mechanisms.definition: Scene-linear color is exposed and mapped through declared preview operators.
mechanisms.integration: Makes output transforms reproducible.

mechanisms.definition: Color-pipeline records may name an OCIO configuration and ACES profile/view.
mechanisms.integration: Interchange target only; this package does not bundle an OCIO runtime.

mechanisms.definition: Opaque, mask and blend modes are explicit material states.
mechanisms.integration: Prevents implicit ordering and collision semantics.

mechanisms.definition: Authoritative simulation advances in fixed dt while input and presentation may use separate clocks.
mechanisms.integration: Makes rollback and event ordering explicit.

mechanisms.definition: Scene, support, relation, motion, interaction and lineage data map to explicit engine components.
mechanisms.integration: Adapter contract; no engine-specific fork is authoritative.

mechanisms.definition: Joints form an acyclic transform hierarchy with inverse-bind and pose data.
mechanisms.integration: Production animation extension; no skinned character is bundled.

mechanisms.definition: Clips, blend states and guarded transitions carry versioned event labels.
mechanisms.integration: Animation events use the same event authority boundary.

mechanisms.definition: The 2.0 damped least-squares IK operator is connected to explicit joint-limit/constraint status.
mechanisms.integration: 2.0 reference implementation retained; 3D production constraints remain application-specific.

mechanisms.definition: Unsupported contacts and dense constraints may be delegated to a conventional physics solver.
mechanisms.integration: Prevents the event substrate from pretending to replace general contact mechanics.

mechanisms.definition: Crossing/impact produces an event; resting contact, joint and grasp use maintained constraints.
mechanisms.integration: Avoids infinite coincident-event emission.

mechanisms.definition: Capsule/shape sweeps return travel fraction, normal, support and compatibility status.
mechanisms.integration: Target interface for playable movement.

mechanisms.definition: Each hand records side, wrist pose, joints, radii, confidence, tracking state, source and timestamp.
mechanisms.integration: Input adapter boundary for XR, mocap or desktop emulation.

mechanisms.definition: Separate enter and exit distances prevent noisy pinch chatter.
mechanisms.formula: enter if d<=d_enter; exit if d>=d_exit, d_exit>d_enter
mechanisms.integration: Produces guarded interaction state with reason codes.

mechanisms.definition: The pair midpoint is the translation anchor for cooperative transforms.
mechanisms.integration: Stable pair frame independent of world origin.

mechanisms.definition: Object scale follows current hand separation relative to anchor separation within clamps.
mechanisms.integration: Supports direct two-hand sizing with a declared degeneracy policy.

mechanisms.definition: Shortest-axis alignment combines with averaged wrist twist around the current pair axis.
mechanisms.formula: q=q_twist*q_align; q_align maps a0 to a1
mechanisms.integration: Provides rotation without Euler-angle discontinuities.

mechanisms.definition: One- and two-hand ownership transitions are an explicit state machine.
mechanisms.integration: Supports join, release and simultaneous-grab events.

mechanisms.definition: When one hand releases a two-hand object, ownership persists under the remaining hand with a lineage label.
mechanisms.integration: Preserves interaction ancestry instead of silently changing controller.

mechanisms.definition: Low-confidence/untracked poses reject transforms; cursor input can emulate the same schema.
mechanisms.integration: Makes XR optional and keeps tests reproducible.

mechanisms.definition: Every committed event receives a monotonic sequence number and pre/post state hashes.
mechanisms.integration: Replication and editor timelines use the same ordering.

mechanisms.definition: Runtime snapshots are hashed and later events can be replayed from the nearest checkpoint.
mechanisms.integration: Reference rollback path for deterministic profiles.

mechanisms.definition: Canonical JSON over schema, scene and runtime counters produces a comparison digest.
mechanisms.integration: Divergence detector; digest is not a replacement for full state.

mechanisms.definition: Peers exchange schema version, mechanism support and asset hashes before authoritative replay.
mechanisms.integration: Production networking contract.

mechanisms.definition: Scene audits, event timelines, culling reasons, lineage edges and runtime metrics are machine-readable.
mechanisms.integration: Makes hidden support/guard/lineage state inspectable.

mechanisms.definition: Replay stops at the first sequence whose expected and actual state hashes differ.
mechanisms.integration: Prevents silent cross-platform desynchronization.

mechanisms.definition: GPU performance claims require a named physical device, driver, workload, precision and equal-error baseline.
mechanisms.formula: promote_claim iff physical_gpu and metrics_complete and oracle_match
mechanisms.integration: Retains the 1.1/2.0 evidence boundary.
